{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''El Paso Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline system in the USA.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2jPLWXM El Paso Gas Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline brings natural gas from the Permian Basin in Texas and the San Juan Basin in New Mexico and Colorado to West Texas, New Mexico, Nevada, California, and Arizona.

==Background==
The El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) pipeline system is owned by Kinder Morgan.<ref name=":0">[http://www.kindermorgan.com/business/gas_pipelines/west/EPNG_MP/ El Paso Natural Gas/Mojave Pipeline], Kinder Morgan, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>  In addition delivering natural gas to West Texas, New Mexico, Nevada, California, and Arizona, it also exports some natural gas to Mexico.<ref name=":0">[http://www.kindermorgan.com/business/gas_pipelines/west/EPNG_MP/ El Paso Natural Gas/Mojave Pipeline], Kinder Morgan, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref> Historically, EPNG's primary market was California, though the growth of competing pipelines into that market and lack of increased demand since 2001 has led to a decrease in its business there, especially in Southern California. At the same time, EPNG's shipping into Arizona has increased, largely because it was the only pipeline into the fast-growing Phoenix area until the TransWestern Phoenix Lateral came in service in 2009. Its largest customers are Southern California Gas Company, a Sempra Energy subsidiary; Southwest Gas Corporation; and Pacific Gas and Electric Company.<ref name=":0"/> Its [[Federal Energy Regulatory Commission|FERC]] code is 33.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130120011541/http://ferc.gov/industries/gas/gen-info/pipecode.asp Three Digit Pipeline Code List for Index of Customers (Form 549B)], FERC, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

From the EPNG website: ''El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is a 10,140-mile pipeline system which transports natural gas from the San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins to California, Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas and Northern Mexico. EPNG also owns approximately 44 billion cubic feet of underground working natural gas storage capacity in Southeast New Mexico.<ref name=":2" />''

==Expansion Projects==
===Carlsbad South Project===
According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the expansion project provides additional takeaway capacity from New Mexico's Permian Basin, to the Pecos, Texas compressor station, and into Keystone pool. The project was completed in February 2021.<ref name="eia1021">[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas, Pipeline Projects], Energy Information Administration, accessed Aug. 16, 2023.</ref>
*'''Operator: ''' El Paso Natural Gas<ref name=eia1021/>
*'''Owner: '''Kinder Morgan Energy Partners<ref name=source1/>
*'''Capacity:''' 159 Mmcf/day<ref name="eia1021" />
*'''Length: '''17.1 miles<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://pipeline2.kindermorgan.com/Documents/EPNG/CP20-483_EPNG_Weekly_Environmental_Report_No._20-20210114151143.pdf|title=EPNG Environmental Report|last=|first=|date=|website=Kinder Morgan|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220110150132/https://pipeline2.kindermorgan.com/Documents/EPNG/CP20-483_EPNG_Weekly_Environmental_Report_No._20-20210114151143.pdf|archive-date=2022-01-10|access-date=2022-01-10}}</ref><ref name="eia1021" />
*'''Diameter: '''16 inches<ref name=":1" />
*'''Cost: '''$23.5 million<ref name="eia1021" />
*'''Status: ''' Operating<ref name=eia1021/>
*'''Start Year: ''' 2021<ref name=eia1021/>


As of December 2021, Carlsbad South Project was listed as complete on the U.S. EIA Natural Gas Pipelines database and began operating the same year.<ref name="eia1021" />

===South Mainline Expansion Project===
According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the expansion project provides additional westbound capacity out of the Waha Hub in Texas and delivers additional supplies (321 million cubic feet per day) to Arizona and Southern California markets. The project was completed in July 2020.<ref name=eia2>[https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=44856 In the first half of 2020, about 5 Bcf/d of natural gas pipeline capacity entered service,] U.S. Energy Information Administration, Aug. 24, 2020, accessed Aug. 17, 2021.</ref>

== Accidents ==
On 19 August 2000, a rupture in the pipeline caused a fire killing 12 campers near Carlsbad, New Mexico. The cause of the rupture was determined to be internal corrosion of the 50-year old transmission pipeline 1103, which had eaten away 70% of the 30-inch diameter pipeline wall.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pstrust.org/map-of-major-incidents/el-paso/|title=El Paso Incident at Carlsbad, New Mexico. 2000|last=|first=|date=|website=Pipeline Safety Trust|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=16 August, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pstrust.org/docs/ntsbcarlsbad.pdf|title=Pipeline Accident Report|last=|first=|date=19 August, 2000|website=Pipeline Safety Trust|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=16 August, 2023}}</ref>

In August 2021, a blast in a portion of the El Paso line 2000 near Coolidge, Arizona killed two people and injured one person. The incident was investigated by U.S. National Transportation Safety Board.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/kinder-sees-blast-damaged-part-arizona-natgas-pipe-down-months-2021-12-01/|title=Kinder sees blast-damaged part of Arizona natgas pipe down for months|work=Reuters|access-date=2023-08-17|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.naturalgasintel.com/el-paso-natural-gas-pipeline-segment-shut-monday-after-deadly-blast/|title=El Paso Natural Gas Pipeline Segment Shut Monday After Deadly Blast|last=Gonzales|first=Leticia|date=16 August, 2021|website=Natural Gas Intel|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=17 August, 2023}}</ref>
